segments.text: Welcome to Daily Robotics, the daily digest of the latest news and developments in the world of robotics.
August 15, 2026, and we've got some exciting stories to share.
From robotics in disaster response, to innovative lift systems, and advancements in autonomous navigation, we've got the inside track on what's new in robotics today.
From thehustle.co, "Cyborg roaches to the rescue?"
Researchers have developed cyborg cockroaches that can survive underwater and in low-oxygen environments, demonstrating a key result in search-and-rescue operations.
The development of these cyborg insects involved the integration of electronic controllers, an oxygen generation tank, and silicone tubes, allowing them to navigate for up to 3 hours.
The cyborg cockroaches were tested during Myanmar's 7.7-magnitude earthquake in March 2025, where they relayed information to identify signs of life.
The success of these tests indicates that the cyborg roaches can potentially be used in future search-and-rescue operations, particularly in environments with limited accessibility.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Lift Happens"
, DARPA's Lift Challenge showcased robots learning to lift and maneuver objects safely, resulting in significant advancements in robotic dexterity and object handling capabilities.

The challenge saw the development and deployment of various robotic systems, including STEMbot, a small robot that successfully climbed plant stems to check for pests, and a new robot from Modlab University of Pennsylvania, which boasted a "truss-worthy" design that enabled stable lifting and manipulation of objects.

Meanwhile, DR02 from DEEP Robotics demonstrated stable movement on stairs, and a miniature robotic structural minifridge was also developed, showcasing the diversity of innovative robotic designs being explored in this field.
"Well, that's a wrap for another day of robot revolution - from cyborg roaches to the rescue, it's clear our insect friends are the ultimate unsung heroes.
Thanks for crawling into the news with us - until tomorrow, robotic dreams!"
